title: The Sound of Silver for the Smell of Sweets (ML)
summary: A greedy confectioner demands payment from a beggar who smelled his sweetmeats. Birbal pays the baker with the clinking sound of coins. [ML]
full_text:
In the sweet bazaar of Agra, a notoriously stingy confectioner named Halwai Chotelal fried fresh, fragrant jalebis in hot clarified butter. A penniless traveler stood on the public street outside the shop, inhaling the delicious aroma while chewing a piece of stale dry bread.

Seeing this, Chotelal grabbed the poor traveler by the collar: 'Pay me five copper coins!'

'For what?' the traveler cried. 'I did not touch your sweets!'

'You stood outside my shop for an hour, enjoying the sweet aroma of my jalebis!' the confectioner yelled. 'The smell belongs to my shop! Pay for the aroma, or I will have you beaten by the watchmen!'

The dispute was dragged before Emperor Akbar, who entrusted the case to Birbal.

Birbal listened to the confectioner's demand with a polite smile: 'Seth Chotelal, you claim that the traveler enjoyed the smell of your sweets, and therefore owes you money?'

'Yes, my lord!' the confectioner beamed. 'Fair payment for fair enjoyment!'

Birbal ordered a brass plate and a purse of twenty silver coins brought from the treasury. Birbal took five silver coins, held them high, and dropped them onto the plate: *Clink-clank-chime!*

The coins bounced on the metal with a bright, musical ring.

Birbal asked: 'Did you hear that sound, Chotelal?'

'Yes, wise minister, loud and clear!'

Birbal dropped the coins a second time: *Clink-clank-chime!*

'Did you enjoy that pleasant sound?'

'Yes, my lord, a wonderful, rich sound!'

Birbal put the coins back into the velvet purse and handed it to the attendant. Turning to the shopkeeper, Birbal said:

'Your debt is settled in full, Chotelal. Just as the traveler enjoyed only the aroma of your food without eating a single bite, so too have you enjoyed the musical sound of his money without keeping a single coin! The smell pays for the bread; the chime pays for the smell!'

The entire court roared with laughter, while the greedy confectioner slunk away in red-faced humiliation.
